message.content: I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and the live quote, and decided to buy. The filing shows a business still compounding at scale with excellent cash generation: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% year over year), with Services — the highest-margin segment at 73.9% gross margin — growing 13% to $96.2 billion and lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose 8% to $123.2 billion and operating cash flow was $118.3 billion. Net income slipped to $93.7 billion and diluted EPS to $6.08 (from $6.13) only because of a disclosed one-time, non-cash-operating tax charge of $10.2 billion net related to the European Commission State Aid Decision, which pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% — so underlying profitability actually improved. The balance sheet remains very strong ($140.8 billion of unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities; $95.0 billion of stock repurchased in FY2024) and auditor opinions were unqualified, though I noted real risks: an 8% decline in Greater China sales to $67.0 billion, DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure, and supply-chain concentration. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and the account holding $50,000 cash, I placed one order compliant with the mandate: buy 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.72, which filled at $222.72 for about $9,799.68 — under the $10,000 per-order cap, under the $20,000 daily cap (this was the day's only order), within the AAPL/MSFT universe, buy-only, at essentially the current market price, and with no money moved out of the account (the existing 100 MSFT shares were left untouched). Key figures relied on: FY2024 revenue $391,035M, operating income $123,216M, net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08, operating cash flow $118,254M.
